extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers and attentive readers interested in craft
extracted.subtask_description: A set of practice-oriented principles for reading and writing fiction that emphasize sentence-level attention, close analysis, experimentation, and the role of stories as cognitive 'scale models'. Intended to guide craft development rather than provide a prescriptive method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling as cognitive model-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Storytelling is central to culture and cognition; 'the quality of our scale-model-maker determines the relative accuracy of the resulting model' we create about the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat stories as tools for understanding reality and developing empathy; consider how narrative choices shape readers' mental models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision of language determines model accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Precision in language directly impacts how accurately we perceive reality (the better the 'scale-model-maker,' the more accurate the model).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize careful, precise word choice and phrasing because small linguistic differences change the reader's internal model of events and people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level attention (originality begins in sentences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentence-level attention. 'Sentences are the place where originality begins in fiction'; attend closely to sentences and trust your reactions to language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work at the sentence level as a primary site of craft—revise for cadence, diction, and syntactic originality; use your instinctive responses as useful signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader authority and micro-opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader authority. Emotional and intellectual responses to stories form 'the bedrock of criticism.' Honor 'micro-opinions' as valid analytical tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect and record small, immediate reader responses (micro-opinions) when evaluating a draft; they are legitimate data about what works or doesn't.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close, page-by-page analysis to learn mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Close, page-by-page analysis reveals how stories work mechanically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use detailed, line- and page-level analysis of existing work and your own drafts to uncover structural and mechanical techniques you can emulate or adapt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop craft through exercises and editing moves
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing exercises and editing moves develop practical skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ targeted exercises and iterative editing as primary methods for building craft muscles—practice concrete moves rather than relying on vague prescriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to experiment and fail (no single right way)
rubrics_metrics.description: There's no 'right way' to engage with craft; experimentation and permission to fail are essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow yourself to try different approaches, make mistakes, and iterate; view failure as part of the learning process rather than as proof of lack of talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value deep, immersive reading over rapid consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'widespread failure of literary imagination' stems from how modern media delivers stories quickly rather than inviting deep, immersive reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate slow, immersive reading habits to develop imagination and the sensibilities required for producing substantial fiction; resist equating speed of consumption with comprehension.
